request.spec:
Show on each person their settled-total (the due of their SETTLED claims that count, at
their frozen figures, corrections included) and their open-total (the due of their OPEN and
PENDING claims that count: a held, deferred or retired-and-excluded claim is left out as it is
from the due-total). Show the sheet's settled-total and open-total too, each simply everyone's
figure added up (not trimmed). The two must add up to the person's untrimmed due-total before the
cap.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each person their settled-total (the due of their SETTLED claims that count, at
their frozen figures, corrections included) and their open-total (the due of their OPEN and
PENDING claims that count: a held, deferred or retired-and-excluded claim is left out as it is
from the due-total). Show the sheet's settled-total and open-total too, each simply everyone's
figure added up (not trimmed). The two must add up to the person's untrimmed due-total before the
cap.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person now shows a settled-total and an open-total, and the sheet shows both totals added up across everyone. All 4 acceptance tests pass in `bin/e2e`.

**What the totals count**
- **Settled-total** is the due of a person's settled claims that count, at their frozen figures. Corrections are included.
- **Open-total** is the due of their open and pending claims that count. Held, deferred and retired-and-excluded claims are left out, the same way the due-total leaves them out.
- The two together add up to the person's due-total before the cap is applied.
- **Sheet totals** are plain sums of everyone's figures, not trimmed of the highest and lowest the way the sheet's due-total is.

**Where the changes are**
- `features/rates/rates.ts`: new `personSplit`, which works out both figures using the same claim figures as the due-total.
- `features/header/totals.ts`: new `useSheetSplit` for the sheet totals.
- `features/rates/rates.slot.tsx`: two new columns on each person row (`person-settled-total`, `person-open-total`), and the sheet totals shown next to the due-total (`rollup-settled-total`, `rollup-open-total`).

This was a front-end-only change: nothing in the stored data or on the server needed to change, and no audit records were added.

One case the tests don't cover: when a person's due-total shows "n/a" (their grade has no rate today and none of their claims has a figure), both new totals show 0.00 rather than n/a.
